[i][u][b]Operation Night Blanketed[/b][/u]

The Kiryusei Socialist Republic launched its surprise invasion of South Kiryusei at 04:03 A.M. on April 24, under Chairman Ren Hoshikais National Reunification Doctrine. The operation, codenamed Crimson Reclaim, began with massive artillery strikes and air raids that shattered Oceanice Enclave Republic border defenses and communication lines. Kiryusei armored divisions and air assault units poured across the Renshou Border, supported by naval bombardments along Tanshi Bay.

Despite the shock assault, the OER South Kiryusei Garrison, comprising over 120,000 troops, quickly regrouped. Typhoon 3500-X and KF-22 fighters countered enemy air formations, while ground and missile units struck advancing columns. The skies and plains of South Kiryusei turned into a fierce battlefield, with both nations suffering severe losses. By nightfall, the frontlines had stabilized amid burning towns and destroyed infrastructure.

On April 25, President Ironvisak Willham addressed the nation, condemning Kiryuseis aggression and declaring full mobilization. OER forces initiated Operation Night Blanketed, launching strategic airstrikes and naval counterattacks to cripple Kiryuseis logistics and regain control of key regions. Intense fighting continued through the next day, with relentless air raids, artillery duels, and naval skirmishes.

After thirty-six hours of nonstop warfare, the conflict reached a brutal stalemate. The Renshou Valley, Harvek Ridge, and Tanshi Bay became entrenched battle zones. Casualties mounted as a result of OER losing over 8,000 troops and dozens of tanks and some military vehicles, while Kiryuseis losses exceeded 12,000 soldiers, and heavy losses from air, land, to sea have left them weakened by OER. Civilians fled as entire towns lay in ruins. By April 26, the Oceanice Enclave Republic prepared Operation Iron Veil, a major counteroffensive to retake occupied ground and push back the Kiryusei advance. The war for South Kiryusei had only begun in a short 2 days in the battle. 

At 04:03 A.M., April 24, 2026, the Socialist regime of Kiryusei attacked our sovereign enclave. They will pay dearly for threatening our freedom and our peoples lives. The OER is ready and united, prepared for this moment. Soon, we will show the world what true freedom and democracy stand for. We call on our EDU brothers to stand with us in this just cause.

Following his speech, the OER mobilized its fleets across the southern and northern seas. Bomber formations of B25-ELX, FK-22, and Eurofighter Typhoon 3500-X swept toward enemy staging areas. Nearly 289,000 active personnel were ordered to reinforce the southern front, as the Oceanice Armed Forces began full-scale wartime operations." -President Ironvisak Willham

Official Statement of the The Kingdom of Ekpatanus 

The Kingdom of Ekpatanus expresses its deep concern over the outbreak of hostilities in South Kiryusei and unequivocally condemns the unprovoked aggression launched by the Kiryusei Socialist Republic under the so-called National Reunification Doctrine. The violation of sovereign borders and the deliberate targeting of civilian infrastructure constitute a grave threat to regional peace and international norms.  

We extend our full solidarity to the Oceanice Enclave Republic and its people, whose resilience and unity in the face of this assault exemplify the enduring strength of democratic nations.  

As a member of the Elseyran Defense Union, Ekpatanus stands firmly with its allies in upholding the principles of sovereignty, freedom, and collective security. In this regard, the Kingdom affirms its readiness to provide any necessary support, including military assistance and direct intervention, should the situation require it.

[b]Amore, pace e felicità[/b]

Among the member nations in the Socialist International, Democratic Sanguivallis stands out by its superficial adherence to liberal democratic ideals. The Social Renaissance Party is indeed the sole ruling party, with a commitment to an eventual transition to communism, though it lacks much of the militant, revolutionary drive often characterized in the works of the First Citharo Conference. The Patriciate, the SRP's [i]de facto[/i] politburo, reflects this current towards tranquility, with [i]Capo[/i] Pio Graci espousing a tendency for practical governance centered not on revolutionary emancipation, but humanistic ideals: [i]Amore, pace e felicità[/i] ("Love, peace, and happiness")

Some call this system overly quixotic, based upon an ideological foundation that perceived the coming utopia of communism as imminent and practical, as a surrender of urgent resolves in order to pursue a fallacious and waiting glory that was now to come upon all countrymen.

However, these charges misunderstand Graci's policy framework.

Sanguivallis is a deeply Catholic nation. Its people fear eternal damnation and long for eternal life. Most agree that life has an innate meaning, that meaning is endowed through the works of a mighty, benevolent, but ineffable Creator, and that therefore what little we understand must be employed in our daily life. Accordingly, any attempts to impose a communist society upon the Sanguinian nation must be done carefully and with deep respect to the values which the country holds dear. Indeed, the Catholic Church itself remains ever-present in the revolution and adheres to the practical philosohy of the Social Renaissance.

The driving justification of the Social Renaissance is this: [i]Dio è, quindi noi dobbiamo essere[/i]. "God is, therefore we must." 

Who is the highest love, the greatest peace, and the purest happiness? God, and so man should be. Accordingly, man should not think for himself but for his family and his neighbor. Under Cui Fang Thought, we think of the exploitation of labor through the historical materialist lens and perceive the crises of capitalism as a deterministic moment. As private markets continue to exploit the worker, the worker in turn becomes more militant. The synthesis of the thesis and antithesis is revolution, the seizure of the means of production, and the dictatorship of the proletariat.

The Social Renaissance, however, operates under the belief that God alone prevails so immensely in the institution of the communist society. Catholic stewardship and option for the poor are not voluntary actions but rather sacred mandates of the believers in the pursuit of good works. The Social Renaissance Party, in this respect, is not a professional and militant vanguard but instead the forcing of God's will on mankind, who dictates the universal moral principles, the cosmic truths of all existence, and the total emancipation of all peoples in all nations. Anything outside of the party, therefore, falls outside the Covenant.

God is, therefore we must. Love, peace, and happiness.

Love one another and be good to your neighbors. Give aid to the poor and contribute to society. Cooperate with grace and inculcate one's self with the virtues of the faith. Preserve the beauty of creation and develop without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. In all things is the social order, not the individual, yet we are individually loved by God.

Find peace when it is possible and impose it when necessary. Wage only just wars in defense of human dignity and this social renaissance. Otherwise, resolve all other issues of society first so that in this tranquility we may observe the withering of the state and the heralding of the communist society.

Happiness is the foremost pursuit of the whole human race. Even those who do not believe in God at least live to have fulfilled the life well-lived. The objective of the state, of human ecology, of the social renaissance, of communism, is the happiness of all men, in the right to basic needs, to education, to labor, and to participation in the revolutionary vanguard.

[b]God is the Revolution[/b]

Pio Graci looked down from the Palazzo dei Cinque and watched as the little figures called men and women proceeded along with their days in the central plaza and in the market squares or within each other's conversation. 

The day was 23 April 2026. During this season of the year that would be called splended spring, the vegetation of Ventusia and the Palazzo seemed rather dead, their fruits withered and leaves discolored into an unhealthy husk. Things have not been kind on Sanguivallis's government since the recent sanctions against its revolutionary government, and so the Patriciate has had to commit to austerity measures after austerity measures to regain market confidence through its allies in the Socialist International.

One such austerity measure have been the mass firings of the Palace's gardeners, once personal servants of the Serenissima itself, but whose wages were paid for by the people who, having instituted the dictatorship of the proletariat, no longer saw the necessity of preserving such audacious displays of bourgeois wealth around the government palace that was meant to be the conduit between the revolution and the state. 

"But things will get better." Pio proclaimed calmly, speaking in an elevated voice for the man behind him. "Ultimately, the fate of all communist governments is to struggle in the dreadful fight against imperialism. All revolutions, even the most tranquil and bloodless ones, have been beset by imperialist backlash to restore the workings of the old. It is why we make compromises and let greed remain for a bit longer."

"The general secretary disagrees, Mr. Graci." Cui Jin flatly explained, his shoulder rising and falling in a simple shrug. "We look at the Serenissima and we look at this current Sanguivallis, but we see little change. You still rule through your Consulate and Patriciate, guided by bourgeois institutions, honor an absent god, and remain committed to ensuring that the economic apparatuses of the state are kept within a wealthy and exploitative neo-feudal class. Mr. Graci, we appreciate the immense support that you have provided the Qianxun Socialist Republic throughout your time post-revolution, but we question whether your state is truly willing and able to commit itself to the Socialist International's program, or whether the collective Sanguinian nation was just a fellow traveler."

"God is the Revolution, Comrade Cui! [i]Solo Dio lo sa![/i]" Pio exclaimed, startling Cui ever so slightly. "Atheists like yourself wallow in despair at a meaningless world but rationalize communism to be the escape. Only God sets us free and liberates us from the shackles of the world! Until then, we emulate His mercy on Earth through the socialist revolution!" 

"If you say so, Mr. Graci."

"I will and I shall a hundred times more. A struggle without spirit is savagery. It's why Comrade Lo Pilato so deeply emphasized the importance of praxis. Everything must be done in terms of their minimums and their maximums. It is as we have discussed at Citharo. Any immediate change brings with it shocks. We cannot immediately impose a maximum program of total revolution over a society that had merely stumbled into liberty. You've built up your capitalist industry to prepare for the transition to socialism, I believe that Sanguivallis has done the same but just on a more careful level."

"If you say so." Cui repeated, having exhausted his side of the debate. "We just wanted assurances that Renaissance Socialism obeys its own rules."

"I'd suggest looking first to our other comrades across the White Straits if you want assurances of world revolution, Comrade Cui." Pio intoned, pointing his finger in the direction of the open waters and the great Vespurian continent that laid there before them. "There are many tens of thousands of workers waiting in Vespuria, and in Thyven, and in Tartakum, Arenenge, Hydronia, and Yonwu who are ready and waiting to begin their own revolution. But they serve dutifully under their liberal democracies, unable or unwilling to take the final push. Today we are triumphing in East Astanir, but it cannot stop there. Love of man and of the world must come to every nation state in existence, and they need our guidance."

"World revolution is good, but first we should make sure we have an idea of what we're doing." Cui replied bluntly, pretending to adjust his collar as he walked close to the [i]Capo[/i], his blank face turning into a visible frown. "We will export the revolution when the time comes. Our cadres in Vespuria grow in number and the popular committees in Astanir have become more radicalized. But the final victory can't come now, not while our general secretary remains wary of our ability to rectify and reaffirm our own policies."

"And what are our policies?"

"We need more cadres. Not just in Vespuria but all across Erene. There are communist parties in Montfleur and Arenenge but who routinely satisfy themselves with minimalist politics. There are militants ready and waiting in Tartakum, in Yonwu, Astanir, and in Vespuria, but they have not yet prosecuted all available means to radicalize their countrymen. In Thyven there are students who idealize the revolution but have no idea how to claim it."

"You're saying things I already know." Pio coolly replied, turning and making direct eye contact with Cui. Crossing his arms, he leaned against the railing of the Palazzo balcony. "What more do you want me to do? The Sanguinian people are still reeling from the fascistic reactions in EDU. I've given you many things in your war against the Daesunics, what more do you wish me to give?"

"You know this isn't my own intent, Comrade Graci. I am merely reflecting the will of my uncle." Cui clarified, sighing quietly. "There's a crisis going on in Vespuria at the moment, comrade. Comrade Almstedt has intervened there as a protector of global capitalism. While I respect the good things he has done for us, at the end of the day he remains a member of the monarcho-fascist elite. The Socialist International wants to take advantage of the chaos to expand the capabilities of Vespuria's Socialist Coalition Party."

"... What do you want me to do?" Pio asked, raising his eyebrow.

"Your [i]Frumentari[/i], Comrade Graci. Consider supplying a few of them to us." Cui answered, making mention of Sanguivallis's intelligence agency. "We are in need of good men to infiltrate every single aspect of Vespurian society to bring to it the socialist revolution all over. Those Midnight Operations so ordered by the Vespurians have caused a multitude of deaths. Entire families have ceased to exist overnight, and with their deaths mean no witnesses capable of appropriately confirming whether they live or not. Birth certificates, death certificates, letters of employment, falsified and true records are all selling like hotcakes, comrade."

"You want the Frumentari to pretend to be Vespurians."

"[i]Bù.[/i] I want them to [i]become [/i] Vespurians, and Thrysmorans, and Montfleurais. Find me agents who have all the features of good Albic men. Pale skin, blue or green eyes, a persistently exhausted countenance if possible. Those that do not will work in the Central Straits. Leave them at Citharo; the Socialist Ethics Commission will do the rest."

Before Pio could muster up a reply or express his reservations, Cui Jin turned around to leave, waving his hand away. The Palazzo then fell into a strange and awkward silence. Pio thought for a bit and wondered that if this great subversion and descecration of the dead was, too, a righteous act of God's revolution. As the sweltering noon Sun approached, however, he resolved to obey the orders of Sanguivallis's greatest patron and departed from the Palazzo later in the hour.

[spoiler=[b]Expectations of Diplomacy[/b]]
On the island of Malce, two men sit on the balcony of a chateau overlooking an ancient vineyard. They ponder recent events between sips of Lavinsworth family wine, a brand which has existed longer than the country they serve. Ah, the weather here is a fine complement to this red. Hopefully recent events will bring me here more often. Looking at his friend, the Intelligence Specialist would smile. Oh how I pity you in that nice ocean view office. Wouldnt want anything but the best? 

Rolling his eyes, the Defence Minister would pour himself another glass before replying. It's simply the change of atmosphere. Everything here seems so heavy with history. Doesnt even feel like were still in Lavia. Pausing for a second, he would ponder such fact, and the history the island would soon see as well. How much longer till the president as well as the diplomat gets here? Witstrom would ask, the topic suddenly coming to the forefront of his mind.

His companion responded bluntly, barely taking his eyes off the commuter ferry on the horizon. The President gets here tomorrow at roughly 0900, and the diplomat follows at roughly at 1300. After another sip of wine, Witstrom would continue his questioning. Think the newly radical diplomat will enjoy us meeting him at such a place like this? He gestured, using his already empty glass to point at the old luxury of the house. 

The other man would smirk a little. Oh please. He was a past diplomat to the Vespurians. Nothing here could top the obnoxious narcissistic opulence which their higher class busies themselves with. Stopping to take a sip of wine, he would continue. I dont believe he is a member of that new insane party there either. Might be the only reasonable person in their whole government now. Witstrom would smile and nod. Right you are Carlos, right you are [/spoiler]

For context, Malce is my Elyseran/Vespurian (can't remember which it belongs to) territory, right under Lamandica. Sorry that it's so short, but I don't have much thought on what to add lol.
